page_refs.doc_date: page 1, last visible row of the table (Sep 17)

scan.summary: This is your own daily pre-shift inspection log for propane forklift FL-2 at the Portland warehouse for September 2026. It is a photo of a sheet, and the bottom of the sheet looks cut off. It shows 11 day-shift checks from Sep 1 to Sep 17, a horn defect on Sep 9 and a propane tank change on Sep 15. This log is your evidence that the truck is checked before each shift and that defects are dealt with, so gaps and loose ends in it weaken that evidence.
scan.freshness_note: The last visible entry is Sep 17, 2026, 10 days before today (Sep 27). The photo is cropped at the bottom edge, so there may be later rows that did not make it into the picture. Ask for the full original sheet, or a photo of the whole page, to see Sep 18 onward.

gaps.title: Truck ran on days with no inspection logged (after Sep 2)
gaps.description: On the other logged days the hour meter goes up about 6–7 hours per shift. Between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834) it went up 15 hours, which is roughly two shifts, most likely Sep 3 and Sep 4. No pre-shift check is recorded for those shifts. (Inferred from the hour-meter readings.)
gaps.fix: Ask the operators whether checks were done on Sep 3–4 and simply not written down. If they were not, note that on the log and remind operators that the check comes before every shift the truck is used. If someone other than M.C. or J.R. uses the truck, they log it too.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), adopted in Oregon through OAR 437-002-0220 (Division 2, Subdivision N). The federal rule requires the check before each shift but does not require it to be written down. The log is your evidence, so gaps weaken it.
gaps.locator: page 1, between the Sep 2 and Sep 7 rows

gaps.title: No entries visible after Sep 17
gaps.description: The last row in the photo is Sep 17. Today is Sep 27, so about seven working days are not shown. The picture is cut off at the bottom, so this may be a photo problem rather than missing checks.
gaps.fix: Get the full sheet or a complete photo. If the checks really stopped after Sep 17, find out why and whether the truck was used.

gaps.title: Horn defect not followed through
gaps.description: On Sep 9 the horn was marked X with the note 'Horn not working'. By Sep 10 the horn is ticked OK and the hour meter rose from 4,847 to 4,853. The log does not say whether the truck was taken out of service on Sep 9, or who repaired the horn and when. The log's own header says not to use the truck if a defect affects safety.
gaps.fix: Find the repair record or work order for the horn and attach it, or add a note on the log with the repair date and who did it. Add a 'defect reported to / corrected on' column so every X has a closing entry.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) (examine before each shift; report and correct defects) and 1910.178(p)(1) (a truck needing repair is taken out of service until restored). Oregon adopts these through OAR 437-002-0220. Oregon also has OAR 437-002-0227, but I have not confirmed that it adds anything about inspection records.
gaps.locator: page 1, Sep 9 row (Horn column and Notes) and Sep 10 row

gaps.title: Operators identified by initials only, no review
gaps.description: Each entry shows only initials (M.C. or J.R.). There is no full name, signature or supervisor sign-off anywhere on the sheet, so it is hard to tie an entry to a trained operator or to show that anyone reviewed the defects.
gaps.fix: Keep a key on the sheet matching initials to full names. Add a supervisor review line, weekly or at month end.
gaps.locator: page 1, Operator column; no review block in the document

facts.value: Toyota 8FGU25 propane forklift, unit FL-2, at the Portland warehouse (the unit number suggests there is at least one other truck; inferred)
facts.affects: Brings in the forklift rules (1910.178 as adopted by Oregon OSHA), including operator training, pre-shift checks and propane refueling and cylinder-change practice

facts.value: Propane (LPG) cylinders used as forklift fuel; cylinders are changed on site
facts.affects: Propane needs to be covered in hazard communication, and cylinder storage and changing need safe-practice and fire-code attention

facts.value: At least two people operate FL-2 (initials M.C. and J.R.). The log does not show whether they are trained or certified.
facts.affects: Each operator needs a training and evaluation certification on file (1910.178(l)), renewed at least every three years
